$comment: Decision-support content (score -> action, result -> action, treatment options with benefit/harm and patient modifiers). Shared by the web (lib/pane-engine/src/decision) and iOS (ios/AmiseMedFlow/Resources/TreatmentDecisions.json, byte-identical copy checked by scripts/src/decision-content-parity.test.ts). EVERY number and wording NEEDS SURGEON SIGN-OFF: sources are cited from memory (fromMemory: true) and effect sizes marked evidence 'estimate' are the author's estimates from the cited trials, not trial results. Clinician-facing suggestions only.

scoreActions.label: Glasgow-Blatchford
scoreActions.riskLabel: risk of needing intervention or death

bands.action: Outpatient management candidate: early discharge without urgent inpatient endoscopy, with safety-net advice and outpatient endoscopy if indicated (NICE CG141: score 0; international consensus 2019 and ESGE 2021: score 0-1).
Admit; endoscopy within 24 h of presentation after resuscitation (NICE CG141; ESGE 2021).
Admit to a monitored bed; resuscitate; endoscopy within 24 h (NICE CG141; ESGE 2021).
Resuscitate and senior review; endoscopy within 24 h, and within 12 h if haemodynamic instability persists after resuscitation (ESGE 2021); consider HDU.
Low risk of rebleeding and death: early discharge with outpatient follow-up (Rockall 1996; NICE CG141).
Intermediate risk: inpatient monitoring after endoscopy; watch for rebleeding (Rockall 1996).
High mortality risk: HDU-level care and senior review; plan for rebleeding (repeat endoscopy, interventional radiology or surgery) (Rockall 1996; ESGE 2021).
Pre-endoscopy Rockall 0: low mortality risk; use the Glasgow-Blatchford score to decide admission and endoscopy timing (NICE CG141).
Pre-endoscopy Rockall >= 1: use the Glasgow-Blatchford score for admission and endoscopy timing; complete the Rockall score after endoscopy (NICE CG141).
Appendicitis unlikely: discharge with safety-net advice, or observe and reassess; the score is used to exclude, not to confirm (WSES 2020).
Equivocal: imaging (ultrasound first; CT in adults if non-diagnostic; MRI in pregnancy) with active observation and rescoring (WSES 2020).
Probable appendicitis: surgical review; imaging before appendicectomy in adults per WSES 2020.
Low probability: outpatient follow-up if the general condition is unaltered (Andersson 2008; WSES 2020).
Indeterminate: in-hospital active observation with rescoring and imaging (Andersson 2008; WSES 2020).
High probability: surgical review for appendicectomy (Andersson 2008; WSES 2020).
Grade I: early laparoscopic cholecystectomy if fit (CCI <= 5 and ASA <= II); otherwise conservative treatment and review (TG18).

Grade II: early laparoscopic cholecystectomy in an experienced centre if fit (CCI <= 5, ASA <= II); otherwise antibiotics with gallbladder drainage if not responding, then delayed cholecystectomy (TG18).

Grade III: organ support and antibiotics; urgent or early gallbladder drainage, unless the organ dysfunction is favourable and the patient is fit for early cholecystectomy in an advanced centre (TG18).
Grade I: antibiotics; biliary drainage if there is no response within 24 h; treat the cause (TG18).
Grade II: early biliary drainage (ERCP) with antibiotics (TG18).
Grade III: organ support, then urgent biliary drainage once stabilised (TG18).
PE unlikely (Wells <= 4): D-dimer; if positive, CTPA (NICE NG158; ESC 2019).
PE likely (Wells > 4): CTPA; interim therapeutic anticoagulation if CTPA is delayed (NICE NG158; ESC 2019).
DVT unlikely (Wells <= 1): D-dimer; if positive, proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (NICE NG158).
DVT likely (Wells >= 2): proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h, with interim anticoagulation if delayed; if negative with a positive D-dimer, repeat the scan at 6-8 days (NICE NG158).
Low severity: consider home treatment; amoxicillin for 5 days per NICE NG138 / local policy.
Moderate severity: consider hospital-based care; amoxicillin, with a macrolide if atypical cover is needed (NICE NG138; CG191).
High severity: hospital admission and critical-care assessment (especially CURB-65 4-5); co-amoxiclav with a macrolide per NICE NG138 / local policy.
A single parameter scoring 3: minimum hourly observations and an urgent ward-based response — the registered nurse informs the medical team (RCP NEWS2 2017).
NEWS2 0: minimum 12-hourly observations (RCP NEWS2 2017).
NEWS2 1-4: minimum 4-6-hourly observations; registered nurse assessment and decision on escalation (RCP NEWS2 2017).
NEWS2 5-6: minimum hourly observations; urgent response by a clinician competent in acute illness; consider sepsis (RCP NEWS2 2017).

NEWS2 >= 7: continuous monitoring and an emergency response by a team with critical-care skills; consider HDU/ICU. In the clinic, call 911 for transfer to the nearest emergency department (RCP NEWS2 2017).
qSOFA < 2 does not exclude sepsis: continue NEWS2 monitoring and reassess if infection is suspected (Sepsis-3; SSC 2021 advises against qSOFA alone as a screening tool).

qSOFA >= 2: high risk of a poor outcome. If suspected infection, treat as sepsis: lactate, blood cultures, IV antibiotics within 1 h, fluid resuscitation guided by perfusion and senior review (SSC 2021); otherwise look for another cause of organ dysfunction.
Very low VTE risk: early mobilisation (ACCP 2012).
Low VTE risk: mechanical prophylaxis, preferably intermittent pneumatic compression (ACCP 2012; NICE NG89).
Moderate VTE risk: LMWH, or mechanical prophylaxis if the bleeding risk is high (ACCP 2012; NICE NG89).
High VTE risk: LMWH plus mechanical prophylaxis; extend to 28 days after major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery (ACCP 2012; NICE NG89).
RCRI 0: no further pre-operative cardiac testing if functional capacity is adequate (ESC/ESAIC 2022).
RCRI 1: ECG; consider NT-proBNP / high-sensitivity troponin before intermediate- or high-risk surgery (ESC/ESAIC 2022; CCS 2017).

RCRI >= 2: ECG and baseline NT-proBNP / high-sensitivity troponin; assess functional capacity; stress imaging only if it would change management; post-operative troponin surveillance (ESC/ESAIC 2022; CCS 2017).
Predicted mild pancreatitis: ward care; moderate goal-directed fluids (WATERFALL 2022); reassess at 48 h.
Predicted severe pancreatitis (Glasgow-Imrie >= 3): HDU / critical-care assessment and close monitoring; CT at 72-96 h if not improving (UK guidelines 2005; IAP/APA 2013).
BISAP 0-2: lower mortality risk; ward care and reassessment at 48 h (Wu 2008).
BISAP >= 3: increased mortality risk — HDU / critical-care assessment and close monitoring (Wu 2008; IAP/APA 2013).
Ranson 0-2: predicted mild pancreatitis; ward care (Ranson 1974).
Ranson >= 3: predicted severe pancreatitis — HDU / critical-care assessment (Ranson 1974; IAP/APA 2013).
LRINEC < 6 does not exclude necrotising soft-tissue infection (low sensitivity): if clinical suspicion persists, urgent surgical exploration (WSES/SIS-E 2018).
LRINEC 6-7: urgent senior surgical review and exploration if suspicion persists; do not delay surgery for imaging (WSES/SIS-E 2018).
LRINEC >= 8: emergency surgical exploration and debridement with broad-spectrum antibiotics including anti-toxin cover (WSES/SIS-E 2018).
HAS-BLED 0-2: low to moderate bleeding risk on anticoagulation (ESC 2020 AF).

HAS-BLED >= 3: high bleeding risk — correct modifiable factors (blood pressure, alcohol, concomitant NSAIDs or antiplatelets, labile INR) and review more often; not by itself a reason to withhold anticoagulation (ESC 2020 AF).
CFS 1-4: not frail; standard peri-operative pathway (CPOC 2021).
CFS 5-6: comprehensive geriatric assessment, delirium prevention and shared decision-making before surgery (CPOC 2021; NICE CG103).
CFS 7-9: goals-of-care discussion and a treatment escalation plan before major surgery; comprehensive geriatric assessment (CPOC 2021; NICE CG103).
NICE NG128 (2019) no longer uses ABCD2 for triage: refer every suspected TIA for specialist assessment within 24 h and start aspirin unless contraindicated (NICE NG128).

resultActions.label: Lipase >= 3 x ULN
resultActions.thresholdText: lipase >= 3 x the upper limit of normal
resultActions.action: Atlanta 2012 biochemical criterion met: with typical epigastric pain (or imaging), acute pancreatitis is diagnosed. Next: severity assessment (SIRS, Glasgow-Imrie at 48 h, BISAP), moderate goal-directed fluid resuscitation (WATERFALL 2022), ultrasound for gallstones, early oral feeding as tolerated.

resultActions.label: Amylase >= 3 x ULN
resultActions.thresholdText: amylase >= 3 x the upper limit of normal
resultActions.action: Atlanta 2012 biochemical criterion met: with typical epigastric pain (or imaging), acute pancreatitis is diagnosed. Next: severity assessment (SIRS, Glasgow-Imrie at 48 h, BISAP), moderate goal-directed fluid resuscitation (WATERFALL 2022), ultrasound for gallstones.

resultActions.label: Troponin above the 99th-centile URL
resultActions.thresholdText: troponin above the assay's 99th-centile upper reference limit
resultActions.action: Acute myocardial injury possible: ECG now; repeat troponin per the ESC 0/1 h or 0/2 h algorithm (or NICE DG40) — a rise or fall confirms acute injury; ACS pathway and cardiology input if ischaemic (ESC 2023).

resultActions.label: Lactate >= 4 mmol/L
resultActions.action: Tissue hypoperfusion: find the cause (sepsis, bleeding, ischaemia, obstructive shock), resuscitate guided by perfusion, repeat lactate within 2-4 h, senior review and critical-care referral. If suspected infection, sepsis bundle now: blood cultures and IV antibiotics within 1 h (SSC 2021).

resultActions.label: Lactate 2-4 mmol/L
resultActions.action: Raised lactate: repeat within 2-4 h and look for sepsis, bleeding or ischaemia (SSC 2021).

resultActions.label: Potassium >= 6.5 mmol/L
resultActions.action: Severe hyperkalaemia: emergency treatment per UKKA 2023 — 12-lead ECG and cardiac monitoring, IV calcium, insulin-glucose and nebulised salbutamol (doses per the UKKA guideline / local policy); treat the cause; repeat K+; renal / critical-care input.

resultActions.label: Potassium 6.0-6.4 mmol/L
resultActions.action: Moderate hyperkalaemia: 12-lead ECG; treat per UKKA 2023 (insulin-glucose; IV calcium if the ECG is abnormal); find and treat the cause; repeat K+.

resultActions.label: Haemoglobin < 70 g/L
resultActions.action: Restrictive transfusion threshold met: consider red cell transfusion, one unit at a time with reassessment (NICE NG24; TRICC 1999; Villanueva 2013 in upper GI bleeding); use 80 g/L with an acute coronary syndrome.

modifiers.label: Age 65-79
modifiers.reason: Older age raises operative morbidity and mortality (NELA; RCS 2018).

modifiers.label: Age 80 or over
modifiers.reason: Age 80 or over raises operative morbidity and mortality (NELA; RCS 2018).

modifiers.label: Age 80 or over
modifiers.reason: Age 80 or over raises procedural complications.

modifiers.label: Age 80 or over
modifiers.reason: Major bleeding with thrombolysis rises with age over 75 (PEITHO; ESC 2019).

modifiers.label: Clinical Frailty Scale 5-6
modifiers.reason: Frailty raises complications and mortality after surgery (ELF 2021; CPOC 2021).

modifiers.label: Clinical Frailty Scale 7 or more
modifiers.reason: Severe frailty strongly raises complications and mortality after surgery (ELF 2021; CPOC 2021).

modifiers.label: Clinical Frailty Scale 5-6
modifiers.reason: Frailty raises procedural complications (CPOC 2021).

modifiers.label: Clinical Frailty Scale 7 or more
modifiers.reason: Severe frailty raises procedural complications (CPOC 2021).

modifiers.label: ASA III
modifiers.reason: ASA III raises operative risk (NELA; TG18 uses ASA to choose early surgery).

modifiers.label: ASA IV or more
modifiers.reason: ASA IV or more strongly raises operative risk (NELA; TG18).

modifiers.label: ASA IV or more
modifiers.reason: ASA IV or more raises procedural and sedation risk.

modifiers.label: eGFR 30-59
modifiers.reason: Renal impairment raises operative risk (NELA).

modifiers.label: eGFR below 30
modifiers.reason: Severe renal impairment raises operative risk (NELA; RCS 2018).

modifiers.label: eGFR below 30
modifiers.reason: Severe renal impairment raises anticoagulant bleeding risk; choose and dose the agent by renal function (ESC 2019; NICE NG158).

modifiers.label: On an oral anticoagulant
modifiers.reason: Anticoagulation needs interruption or reversal and raises bleeding (ACCP 2022; ESC/ESAIC 2022).

modifiers.label: On an oral anticoagulant
modifiers.reason: Oral anticoagulation is a relative contraindication to thrombolysis (ESC 2019).

modifiers.label: On antiplatelet therapy
modifiers.reason: Antiplatelet therapy adds to anticoagulant and thrombolytic bleeding (ESC 2019).

modifiers.label: HAS-BLED 3 or more
modifiers.reason: High bleeding risk on anticoagulation (HAS-BLED; ESC 2020).

modifiers.label: Pregnant
modifiers.reason: Surgery in pregnancy carries fetal loss and preterm-labour risk; obstetric involvement (ACOG CO 775).

modifiers.label: Pregnant
modifiers.reason: Pregnancy is a relative contraindication to thrombolysis (ESC 2019).

modifiers.label: Penicillin allergy recorded
modifiers.reason: The usual regimen contains a penicillin: use a non-penicillin regimen per local policy; second-line regimens carry more adverse effects (Blumenthal 2018).

modifiers.label: Diabetes
modifiers.reason: Diabetes raises surgical-site infection and peri-operative complications (CPOC 2021).

modifiers.label: Immunosuppressed
modifiers.reason: Immunosuppression raises infective and healing complications.

modifiers.label: BMI 40 or more
modifiers.reason: Severe obesity raises operative and anaesthetic complications.

modifiers.label: NEWS2 7 or more
modifiers.reason: Physiological derangement raises peri-operative risk (NELA; RCS 2018).

modifiers.label: Shock (SBP < 90 or lactate >= 4)
modifiers.reason: Shock raises operative mortality (NELA).

modifiers.label: Surgery within 21 days
modifiers.reason: Recent surgery raises anticoagulant bleeding risk (ESC 2019).

modifiers.label: Surgery within 21 days
modifiers.reason: Major surgery or trauma within 3 weeks is a contraindication to systemic thrombolysis (ESC 2019): catheter-directed treatment or surgical embolectomy instead.

test.label: CT abdomen/pelvis in adults (ultrasound first in children and in pregnancy, MRI if non-diagnostic)

options.label: Laparoscopic appendicectomy
options.planLine: Laparoscopic appendicectomy (WSES 2020): consent, antibiotic prophylaxis per local policy, VTE risk assessment.
options.observeText: Active observation with repeat clinical assessment, rescoring and imaging (WSES 2020).

options.label: Antibiotics-first (non-operative)
options.planLine: Antibiotics-first for imaging-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis without an appendicolith: IV then oral antibiotics per local policy; explain that about 3 in 10 need appendicectomy within 90 days (CODA 2020) and about 4 in 10 by 5 years (APPAC).

modifiers.label: Pregnant
modifiers.reason: Pregnancy was excluded from CODA and APPAC; failure risks perforation and fetal loss, so appendicectomy is preferred (WSES 2020).

modifiers.label: Appendicolith on imaging
modifiers.reason: An appendicolith raises antibiotic failure (CODA 2020: about 4 in 10 vs 2.5 in 10 needed appendicectomy).

options.label: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy
options.planLine: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy (within 72 h of admission, same admission) if fit — TG18 (CCI <= 5, ASA <= II) and CHOCOLATE 2018.
options.observeText: Antibiotics and supportive care; delayed cholecystectomy if fit later (TG18).

options.label: Percutaneous cholecystostomy (gallbladder drainage)
options.planLine: Percutaneous cholecystostomy for patients unfit for early surgery or not responding to antibiotics (TG18), with a later decision on interval cholecystectomy.
options.observeText: Antibiotics and supportive care with close review (TG18).

options.label: Antibiotics and supportive care alone
options.planLine: Antibiotics per local policy with analgesia, fluids and review; escalate to drainage if not improving within 24-48 h (TG18).

options.label: Antibiotics
options.planLine: Antibiotics per local antimicrobial policy — for immunocompromised, systemically unwell or not-improving patients (WSES 2020; AVOD; DIABOLO).
options.observeText: Observation without antibiotics: analgesia, oral fluids, safety-net advice and review (DIABOLO 2017; AVOD 2012; WSES 2020).

options.label: Hospital admission
options.planLine: Admit for IV fluids, analgesia and monitoring; antibiotics per local policy if indicated (WSES 2020).
options.observeText: Outpatient management with safety-net advice and early review if tolerating oral intake (DINAMO 2021; WSES 2020).

modifiers.label: Immunosuppressed
modifiers.reason: Immunocompromised patients were excluded from DIABOLO/AVOD; antibiotics are advised (WSES 2020).

modifiers.label: Immunosuppressed
modifiers.reason: Immunosuppression favours admission (WSES 2020).

modifiers.label: Age 80 or over
modifiers.reason: Older patients were under-represented in outpatient trials; lower threshold to admit (WSES 2020).

modifiers.label: Clinical Frailty Scale 7 or more
modifiers.reason: Severe frailty favours admission.

modifiers.label: NEWS2 7 or more
modifiers.reason: Systemic illness needs admission (WSES 2020; RCP NEWS2).

modifiers.label: Shock (SBP < 90 or lactate >= 4)
modifiers.reason: Shock needs admission and resuscitation.

modifiers.label: Shock (SBP < 90 or lactate >= 4)
modifiers.reason: Sepsis needs antibiotics (SSC 2021).

decisions.label: Upper GI bleeding — admission and endoscopy timing

options.label: Admission and endoscopy within 24 h
options.planLine: Admit; endoscopy within 24 h of presentation after resuscitation (NICE CG141; ESGE 2021).
options.observeText: Outpatient management without urgent inpatient endoscopy (Glasgow-Blatchford 0-1: NICE CG141; international consensus 2019), with safety-net advice and outpatient endoscopy if indicated.

options.label: Endoscopy within 12 h (after resuscitation)
options.planLine: Endoscopy within 12 h after haemodynamic resuscitation — for haemodynamic instability persisting after resuscitation (ESGE 2021).
options.observeText: Endoscopy within 24 h: urgent (< 6 h) endoscopy did not lower mortality in high-risk patients without persisting shock (Lau 2020).

modifiers.label: Shock (SBP < 90 or lactate >= 4)
modifiers.reason: Haemodynamic instability persisting after resuscitation: endoscopy within 12 h (ESGE 2021).

test.label: CT pulmonary angiography (D-dimer first if PE is unlikely; V/Q or leg ultrasound in pregnancy per local protocol)

options.label: Therapeutic anticoagulation
options.planLine: Therapeutic anticoagulation per ESC 2019 / NICE NG158 — agent chosen for renal function, pregnancy, cancer and bleeding risk; interim anticoagulation if imaging is delayed.
options.observeText: No anticoagulation while PE is unlikely or excluded; complete the diagnostic pathway.

options.label: Systemic thrombolysis
options.planLine: Systemic thrombolysis for high-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE after checking contraindications (ESC 2019).
options.observeText: No thrombolysis: anticoagulate and monitor; rescue reperfusion if haemodynamic decompensation (ESC 2019; PEITHO 2014).

modifiers.label: Shock (SBP < 90 or lactate >= 4)
modifiers.reason: High-risk PE with shock: systemic thrombolysis is recommended (ESC 2019).

options.label: Pharmacological prophylaxis (LMWH) with mechanical prophylaxis
options.planLine: VTE prophylaxis: LMWH (renal-adjusted) with mechanical prophylaxis unless contraindicated (NICE NG89; ACCP 2012).
options.observeText: Early mobilisation, with mechanical prophylaxis where indicated (ACCP 2012).

options.label: Mechanical prophylaxis
options.planLine: Mechanical VTE prophylaxis: intermittent pneumatic compression (or anti-embolism stockings unless contraindicated, e.g. peripheral arterial disease) (NICE NG89).
options.observeText: Early mobilisation only (ACCP 2012: very low risk).

modifiers.label: On therapeutic anticoagulation
modifiers.reason: Already on therapeutic anticoagulation: see the anticoagulation plan instead of prophylactic LMWH (NICE NG89).

options.label: IV antibiotics within 1 hour
options.planLine: IV antibiotics within 1 hour of recognition, after blood cultures (SSC 2021: shock or high likelihood of sepsis).
options.observeText: Rapid assessment for infection; if concern persists, antibiotics within 3 hours (SSC 2021: possible sepsis without shock).

modifiers.label: Shock (SBP < 90 or lactate >= 4)
modifiers.reason: In septic shock each hour of delay raises mortality: antibiotics within 1 h (SSC 2021; Kumar 2006).

options.label: Elective inguinal hernia repair
options.planLine: Elective inguinal hernia repair with mesh, laparoscopic or open (HerniaSurge 2018).
options.observeText: Watchful waiting for a minimally symptomatic hernia in men, with advice on incarceration symptoms (HerniaSurge 2018; Fitzgibbons 2006; O'Dwyer 2006).

decisions.label: Acute gallstone pancreatitis — timing of cholecystectomy

options.label: Same-admission laparoscopic cholecystectomy
options.planLine: Same-admission laparoscopic cholecystectomy for mild gallstone pancreatitis (PONCHO 2015).
options.observeText: Interval cholecystectomy; in severe or necrotising pancreatitis defer until collections resolve or for at least 6 weeks (IAP/APA 2013).
options.note: Applies when the pancreatitis is gallstone-related.

modifiers.label: Predicted severe pancreatitis (Glasgow-Imrie, BISAP or Ranson >= 3)
modifiers.reason: Severe pancreatitis: defer cholecystectomy until collections resolve or for at least 6 weeks (IAP/APA 2013).

options.label: Emergency laparotomy
options.planLine: Emergency laparotomy for source control: document the NELA (or P-POSSUM) mortality risk; if >= 5%, consultant surgeon and anaesthetist present and planned critical care (NELA; RCS 2018).
options.observeText: Non-operative or palliative management — only after a documented senior discussion of goals of care with the patient and family (CPOC 2021; NELA).

riskFactors.label: Mechanical heart valve (high thromboembolic risk; weighted for valve thrombosis — estimate)
VTE within 3 months (high thromboembolic risk — estimate)

options.label: Bridging with therapeutic-dose LMWH
options.planLine: Bridging with therapeutic-dose LMWH during warfarin interruption — for a mechanical valve, VTE within 3 months or a high-risk thrombophilia, planned with cardiology / haematology (ACCP 2022; ACC/AHA 2020).
options.observeText: No bridging: interrupt and restart the anticoagulant per the peri-procedural plan (BRIDGE 2015; PAUSE 2019; ACCP 2022).

modifiers.label: On a DOAC (not warfarin)
modifiers.reason: No bridging with a DOAC: interrupt and restart per PAUSE 2019 (ACCP 2022).

cfs.label: Clinical Frailty Scale
cfs.effect: frailty raises the harm of operations and procedures

egfr.label: eGFR
egfr.effect: eGFR below 30 raises operative and anticoagulant harm

pregnancy.label: pregnancy status
pregnancy.effect: pregnancy changes the harm of operations and thrombolysis and excludes some options

bmi.label: BMI (height and weight)
bmi.effect: BMI 40 or more raises operative harm

hasBled.label: HAS-BLED
hasBled.effect: HAS-BLED 3 or more raises anticoagulant bleeding

news2.label: a full set of observations (NEWS2)
news2.effect: NEWS2 7 or more or shock changes the balance
